facts.value: ASU offers direct admission for nearly all majors, which means students are directly admitted as long as they meet applicable admission requirements for both ASU and their major and complete the steps to apply.
A transfer student is anyone who has attended another college or university and has completed 12 or more transferable credits post-high school at the time of applying to Arizona State University.
The minimum GPA for transfer admission consideration at ASU is typically around 2.50.
Transfer students with 12–23 transferable credits (post-high school) must have a minimum 2.50 cumulative transfer GPA and meet first-year student admission requirements.
Applying to ASU only takes about 30 minutes.
You’ll get an admission decision within 10 days if you self-report your grades, but it may take a little longer if your transcript is sent directly.
Tuition and fees vary depending on your program.
ASU may offer conditional admission to international applicants who meet the academic requirements but are not proficient in English.
International F-1 students have three semesters to submit a passing TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE score, or to successfully graduate from ASU Global Launch to be fully admitted to the university.
